_comment: Real Miami University (Oxford) buildings, current and past, compiled from the cited public sources on 2026-09-30. NOTHING here has been checked against University Archives records: every entry is verified:false. confidence: corroborated = 2+ sources agree; sourced = one source; conflicting = sources disagree (see notes); estimate = decade/circa only; unknown = no date found. Scope: university-owned or -used buildings and landmarks (incl. Western College and Oxford College buildings), not fraternity houses or private homes. osm_id links a standing building to its present-day footprint; site is for buildings with no OSM outline (filled in Spike B 3c).

entries.name: DeWitt Log Homestead
entries.notes: Oldest extant structure in Oxford Township (NRHP 1973). Miami ownership / campus status unverified.

entries.name: Old Main
entries.notes: Construction began 1816; central part completed 1818. Replaced on the same site by Harrison Hall (1960). Drawn on the footprint of Harrison Hall (same site; approximate outline).

entries.name: Elliott Hall
entries.notes: Miami's timeline: 'constructed' 1828. Wikipedia: built 1825. NRHP lists 1829 as a significant year. First residence hall (North Hall).

entries.name: Scott House (2 South Campus Avenue)
entries.notes: Birthplace of Caroline Scott Harrison. Part of Miami's cottage system in the mid-1920s; current Miami ownership unverified.

entries.name: William H. McGuffey House
entries.notes: Walking tour: ca. 1832–33. Museum; National Historic Landmark.

entries.name: Bishop House (400 East High Street)
entries.notes: Home of Miami's first president Robert Hamilton Bishop 1836–45. Acquired by Miami 1929; razed 1960.

entries.name: Simpson-Shade Guest House
entries.notes: Built about 1836 (Rogers House). Given to Miami 1930; renamed Simpson-Shade 2004.

entries.name: Stoddard Hall
entries.notes: Miami's timeline and Wikipedia: 1836. NRHP lists 1835 as a significant year. Second residence hall (South Hall).

entries.name: Kennedy House (322 East High Street)
entries.notes: 'Probably constructed by 1839'. Purchased by Miami about a decade before it was destroyed by arson in 1978.

entries.name: Lewis Place
entries.notes: Leased to Miami 1903, sold to Miami 1929; official residence of Miami presidents. Largest addition 2007.

entries.name: Richey House (220 East High Street)
entries.notes: Walking tour: 'beginning in the mid-1840s'. Given to Miami 1988; used as housing for administrators.

entries.name: Oxford College for Women (Oxford Female Institute building)

events.event: acquired by Miami; main building renovated

entries.notes: Acquired by Miami 1928 and renovated; now the Oxford Community Arts Center (leased/transferred; current ownership unverified).

entries.name: Old Manse
entries.notes: 'Coffee Mill House'. Presbyterian parsonage 1883–1956; Miami property from 1973 (Wikipedia).

entries.name: Langstroth Cottage
entries.notes: Miami's timeline and Wikipedia text: 1856; Wikipedia infobox: 1858. National Historic Landmark (1976).

entries.name: Bonham House
entries.notes: Built for Miami president Robert Stanton. Home of the Myaamia Center.

entries.name: Peabody Hall
entries.notes: Original Seminary Hall built 1855, burned 1860, rebuilt 1861, burned 1871 and rebuilt the same year; named Peabody Hall 1905. Miami's timeline gives '1860/1871'.

entries.name: Tenney Gateway
entries.notes: Miami's timeline: '1890s'.

entries.name: Alumnae Hall (Western College)
entries.notes: Western's library until 1970; scheduled to be razed 1975, torn down 1977.

entries.name: Brice Scientific Hall
entries.notes: Constructed for science instruction. Later history / demolition not found.

entries.name: Lutheran Parsonage (221 East Spring Street)
entries.notes: Built about 1896; removed after Miami acquired it (year not stated).

entries.name: Miami Field
entries.notes: Opened 1896 as Athletic Park (Yager Stadium article says in use since 1895). Closed 1982; site of the Biological Sciences Building (Pearson Hall).

entries.name: Herron Gymnasium
entries.notes: Later Van Voorhis Hall; NRHP 1979. (A 2025 Miami Student article's claim that it was cleared for Ogden Hall conflicts with this.)

entries.name: McKee Hall
entries.notes: Named McKee Hall in 1917 (formerly 'New Hall').

entries.name: Huston House (215 East Spring Street)
entries.notes: Sold to Miami 1947; sold in 1963 and moved several miles west of Oxford. Site now the western part of Hanna House.

entries.name: Hall Auditorium
entries.notes: Built as the Administration/Auditorium Building; renamed Benton Hall 1926, Hall Auditorium 1969.

entries.name: Tallawanda Apartments (Tallawanda Hall)
entries.notes: Built privately by Miami faculty; Miami purchased it in 1952 as a women's residence hall ('Tallawanda Hall acquired'). Now a parking lot; demolition year not found.

entries.name: McGuffey Hall
entries.notes: Built as the Normal College's South Pavilion; wings 1915, 1916 and 1925.

entries.name: Alumni Hall
entries.notes: Wikipedia: completed 1910; Miami's timeline lists it under 1909 (Carnegie award). Renamed from Alumni Library to Alumni Hall when King Library was completed (1972). Chose 1910: 1909 appears to be the year of the Carnegie award, not completion.

entries.name: Joyner House
entries.notes: Herald House in the 1920s; sold to Miami 1967; demolition began June 2026 (WCPO).

entries.name: New Cottage and South Cottage
entries.notes: Temporary women's housing 'for about a dozen years' before Wells Hall was built on the site in 1923.

entries.name: Stafford House (216 East High Street)
entries.notes: Acquired by Miami 2007, razed 2008.

entries.name: Bishop Hall
entries.notes: Built as a residence for women (construction began 1911).

entries.name: Kumler Chapel
entries.notes: Built 1917–18; architect Thomas Hastings.

entries.name: Western Campus bridges
entries.notes: Miami's timeline: '1920s'.

entries.name: Wells Hall
entries.notes: Built 1922–23 as a residence for women; last used 2019; demolition began June 2026 (WCPO).

entries.name: New Freshman Dormitory (1924)
entries.notes: Listed as 'constructed as residence for men'; later name not established.

entries.name: Ogden Hall
entries.notes: Residence for men and student center; construction began 1923; renovated and extended 1999.

entries.name: University Hospital (1924)
entries.notes: Relationship to the later MacMillan Hospital / MacMillan Hall not established.

entries.name: Irvin Hall
entries.notes: Constructed as a recitation building.

entries.name: Wilson Hall
entries.notes: Built as 'The Pines', an annex of the Oxford Retreat; sold to Miami 1936; renamed Wilson Hall 1986; demolition approved Feb 2019 for that summer (completion not separately confirmed).

entries.name: Corson House
entries.notes: Miami's timeline: '1930s'.

entries.name: Kreger Hall
entries.notes: Built as the center section of Hughes Hall for chemistry; now Kreger Hall. Reopened 2014 with a new wing for physics.

entries.name: Presser Hall
entries.notes: Listed among the Western College buildings acquired in 1974.

entries.name: Withrow Court
entries.notes: Miami's timeline: constructed 1931; Wikipedia: inaugurated Feb 1932. Closed 2016. Wikipedia says it was repurposed into Withrow Hall; Miami's 2016–17 parking map ('Withrow Court Demolition') and 2018 news ('built on site of original Withrow Court') indicate demolition and a new building. Drawn on the footprint of Withrow Hall (same site; approximate outline).

entries.name: Richard Hall
entries.notes: Wikipedia: built 1940 as 'South Hall'; Miami's timeline: 1941. New wing and renamed Richard Hall 6 Dec 1952. Chose 1940: Wikipedia gives construction details (north unit built 1940, $220,000).
